card: Explicitly marks accepted P2P and HTTP server sockets as non-blocking. On Linux, accepted sockets do not inherit O_NONBLOCK from listening sockets, creating potential stalling vulnerabilities if any send or recv operation misses MSG_DONTWAIT. The author characterizes this as a defense-in-depth safeguard against remote socket-blocking denial-of-service issues. It has no dependencies.
changed_since_previous: Diff provided (previously nopatch); no functional changes to the proposed solution.
evidence: Author description: "A mistake here would be critical, as it would allow a malicious peer to stall us indefinitely for free. This is not currently an issue because... on Linux/macOS/BSD [we use] MSG_DONTWAIT; while on Windows MSG_DONTWAIT is unset, accepted sockets do inherit the non-blocking option."

Commit baf93e8ffd: "a mistake here would be critical and the belt-and-suspenders check does not cost anything (we even have an unnecessary one for TCP_NODELAY, which *is* inherited on all of Linux/macOS/BSD/Windows)."
problem: On Linux, accepted sockets do not inherit the O_NONBLOCK status flag from the listening socket. Currently, nodes avoid blocking because send and receive calls on POSIX platforms explicitly use MSG_DONTWAIT, but relying entirely on per-call flags risks stalls if any I/O call omits the flag.

risk.why: If setting non-blocking fails or behaves unexpectedly on a supported platform, inbound P2P connections or HTTP RPC requests will be rejected.

summary: Explicitly sets accepted sockets for inbound P2P connections and HTTP clients to non-blocking mode immediately after acceptance. If setting the socket to non-blocking fails, the connection is aborted with a warning log.
